History & Physical (Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
32-year-old male with 6-week history of intermittent left-sided hearing reduction, tinnitus, and mild disequilibrium; no pain or discharge. Video visit arranged an in-person otoscopic examination to rule out cerumen impaction and other pathology.

History:
• Presenting complaint: “Can’t really hear as well as I used to” in the left ear.  
• Onset & course: Began ~6 weeks ago; intermittent; fluctuates day-to-day.  
• Laterality: Unilateral—left ear only; right ear normal.  
• Associated symptoms  
  – Intermittent ringing (tinnitus) in left ear; less noticeable when TV/music playing.  
  – Occasional mild dizziness / feeling “off balance”; not true vertigo; no nausea.  
  – Denies ear pain, otorrhea, pruritus, fever, chest pain, palpitations.  
• Exacerbating / relieving factors: Background noise (TV, music) masks tinnitus; no other specific triggers reported.  
• Prior similar episode: Brief 2-day hearing difficulty about 1 year ago, resolved spontaneously.  
• Review of systems (pertinent negatives): No upper-respiratory symptoms, headache, visual changes, neurological deficits, or trauma reported.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions reported.  
• Prior brief unilateral hearing difficulty 1 year ago (self-resolved).  
Medications: None mentioned.  
Allergies: Not discussed.

Social History:
• Privacy confirmed during call.  
• No information provided on occupation, noise exposure, smoking, alcohol, or recreational drug use.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• Virtual visit—no vitals or physical findings documented.

Investigations:
• None to date.  
• Plan: Face-to-face clinic visit within 4–5 days for otoscopic examination to rule out cerumen impaction or other external/middle-ear pathology.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Left-sided hearing loss with tinnitus ± mild disequilibrium  
  Assessment: Likely conductive cause such as cerumen impaction, but inner/middle-ear causes (e.g., Ménière’s disease, serous otitis media, acoustic neuroma) also considered.  
  Plan:  
  • Schedule in-person otoscopy and ear canal inspection (appointment arranged via support team).  
  • If cerumen impaction present: remove wax (e.g., irrigation or microsuction) per in-clinic protocol.  
  • Provide patient education—link to tinnitus information leaflet placed in notes.  
  • Safety-net: If symptoms worsen (e.g., true vertigo, severe hearing loss, new neurological signs) before appointment, patient to book urgent review or ED attendance.  

General:  
  • No medications started at this visit.  
  • Follow-up after examination to review findings and determine further management (e.g., audiogram, ENT referral) as needed.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Cerumen impaction – High likelihood: common cause of unilateral muffled hearing; planned otoscopy to confirm/exclude.  
2. Ménière’s disease – Moderate likelihood: unilateral fluctuating hearing loss + tinnitus + disequilibrium, though vertigo is mild and continuous.  
3. Serous otitis media / Eustachian-tube dysfunction – Moderate likelihood: gradual conductive loss and tinnitus without pain or fever; no URI reported but still possible.

Quality checks:
• Missing but expected: allergies, current medication list, occupation/noise exposure, smoking/alcohol history, vitals, full ENT/neurologic exam.  
• Conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; occasional short patient responses but overall adequate for documentation.
